title: Ribociclib derivative Rib-CA suppresses breast cancer progression via p53-dependent apoptosis.
authors: Song, Mengwei; Zhou, Ying; Yu, Xudong; Zhang, Boyu; Wang, Sen; Asan, Kadirya; Yang, Zihao; Lin, Haiyan; Wang, Jian; Song, Xiaoxue; Jiang, Yongyuan; Chen, Si; Ji, Jing; XiujunWang; Mou, Yi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究新型CDK4/6抑制剂衍生物的抗乳腺癌作用及p53凋亡机制，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Breast cancer is a major global health challenge with high incidence and mortality. CDK4/6 inhibitors like Ribociclib have shown clinical benefits, but drug resistance remains a limitation. We designed and synthesized a novel Ribociclib derivative, Rib-CA, and evaluated its antitumor effects using in vitro assays (MTT, colony formation, EdU incorporation, cell adhesion, Transwell invasion, and wound healing) and in vivo models (CAM assay, xenografts). Transcriptomics, Western blotting, and machine learning were employed to explore its mechanism. Pharmacokinetics and safety were assessed via ADMETlab 2.0. Rib-CA exhibited enhanced anti-proliferative and anti-metastatic effects in MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7 cells compared to Ribociclib. Mechanistically, it activated p53 signaling, induced apoptosis, and triggered G2/M arrest. Machine learning identified CACHD1 and LAGE3 as potential biomarkers linked to p53 and immune regulation. In vivo, Rib-CA suppressed tumor growth and angiogenesis more effectively than Ribociclib, with favorable pharmacokinetics. Rib-CA demonstrates enhanced antitumor activity through p53 pathway activation and metastasis suppression, suggesting its therapeutic potential for breast cancer treatment.
abstract_zh: 乳腺癌是全球重大健康挑战，发病率和死亡率均较高。CDK4/6抑制剂如Ribociclib已显示出临床获益，但耐药性仍是其局限性。我们设计并合成了一种新型Ribociclib衍生物Rib-CA，并通过体外实验（MTT、集落形成、EdU掺入、细胞粘附、Transwell侵袭和伤口愈合）及体内模型（CAM实验、异种移植瘤）评估其抗肿瘤效果。采用转录组学、Western blotting和机器学习探讨其机制，并通过ADMETlab 2.0评估药代动力学和安全性。与Ribociclib相比，Rib-CA在MDA-MB-231和MCF-7细胞中表现出增强的抗增殖和抗转移作用。机制上，它激活p53信号通路，诱导凋亡，并触发G2/M期阻滞。机器学习识别出CACHD1和LAGE3为与p53及免疫调节相关的潜在生物标志物。在体内，Rib-CA比Ribociclib更有效地抑制肿瘤生长和血管生成，且药代动力学特性良好。Rib-CA通过p53通路激活和转移抑制展现出增强的抗肿瘤活性，提示其在乳腺癌治疗中的潜在应用价值。
